# Section coverage of the Union-level Acts (generated by `scan/section_coverage.py`; do not edit by hand)

Measured on the served collection `kanoon_v1` (74,484 Union-level Act points, the copy instance, 5 Nov 2026). Free, read-only, no model calls. Method and limits are in the module docstring of `scan/section_coverage.py`.

## Headline

| | Acts | Sections expected (lower bound) | Chunk labelled with the number | No chunk labelled | ...of which the text is inside the chunk before | **Likely absent** | Share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All Union-level Acts | 1,568 | 59,053 | 35,371 | 23,682 | 2,590 | **21,092** | **35.7%** |
| In force | 848 | 38,294 | 28,710 | 9,584 | 1,733 | **7,851** | **20.5%** |
| Repealed | 710 | 20,547 | 6,497 | 14,050 | 854 | **13,196** | **64.2%** |
| Spent | 10 | 212 | 164 | 48 | 3 | **45** | **21.2%** |

In force: **734 of 848 Acts lack a chunk for at least one section number** (only 114 have every number from 1 to N); 154 hold fewer than half of the labels they should; 77 are missing a section that other sections of the same Act cite at least 3 times; 50 have a shared number that is also cited that often. Structure of the Acts in force: {'labelled': 787, 'stub': 45, 'no labels': 16}.

`no labels` = the Act is stored as unlabelled text blocks (a lookup by section number finds nothing, though the text may be searchable); `stub` = 1 to 3 labelled sections in an Act that should have 10 or more; `labelled` = the rest.

## How far to trust these numbers

* **The same method, run independently, agrees.** The owner's earlier checker (`lexbharat-merge`, W10, on that repo's own copy of the data) found, for Acts in force, 38,508 sections expected and 8,881 missing; this scan finds 38,294 expected and 9,584 with no chunk labelled. For all 1,568 Acts it found 68,822 expected and 32,425 missing; this scan finds fewer because a year filed as a section number is no longer counted as one.
* **N is a lower bound**, so a shortfall of a tail (sections beyond the highest number held) is invisible. Schedule rows filed as sections can push N up, and an omitted or repealed section number counts as missing; both make the missing count too high.
* **'Text inside the chunk before'** credits a missing number when its heading is found inside a chunk labelled 1 to 3 numbers lower (the chunker appends an amended or substituted section to the one before it). Hand-checked on three known cases (IPC 34 inside the chunk labelled 33, NDPS 37 inside 36C, Registration Act 49 inside 48) and on 16 random credits: 13 were the real section's heading, 3 were not (a footnote, an amendment-table row, a list), so the credit slightly over-states what is present. **The honest range for sections with no text anywhere is therefore the 'Likely absent' figure up to the 'No chunk labelled' figure.**
* **Not detected:** a number that is labelled and shared by Order or Schedule rules while the section's own text is absent (CPC 9 and 11). Those appear only in the shared-number table below.
* **Not measured:** whether a labelled section's text is complete. The holes are in the source: the parquet has 1,098,269 rows against 1,098,577 points in `acts_india` (Central: 25 more points than rows, none fewer; DATA-GAPS section 20), so the holes are in the source file and were not lost in indexing.
